title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 121
text:
109. Assessment by an intermediary should be considered if the person seems unlikely to be able
to recognise a problematic question or, even if able to do so, may be reluctant to say so to a
questioner in a position of authority. Studies suggest that the majority of young witnesses
across all ages fall into one or other or both categories.

110. Whether young witnesses should have an intermediary assessment should be decided
with care on an individual basis. The language comprehension of a young witness, no
matter how advanced they appear, is likely to be less than that of an adult witness.

111. A deaf person should always be assessed by an expert in deafness and/or a suitably
qualified and experienced intermediary.
76

112. Intermediaries have a role and specialism which is sometimes essential for a fair
hearing. Notwithstanding this, the court can and should play a significant role in
facilitating questioning.
